brief.subject: Fake passport help sites, a $106.8M debt relief ruling
brief.headline: FTC Targets Fake Passport Help Sites; Court Shuts Debt Relief Scheme
brief.dek: Regulators act against government impersonators selling passport services and a debt relief operation that targeted seniors and veterans.
brief.lede: The FTC has sued operators accused of posing as the government to sell passport services through paid search ads. Before paying for any passport help, confirm you are on an official government site.

sections.heading: Fake Government Passport Help
bullets: The FTC sued GovAssist LLC, Entry LLC and Scott Zuckerman over an alleged government impersonation scheme.
Consumers seeking passport services were allegedly misled into thinking the operation was, or was tied to, the federal government.
Paid search ads were allegedly used to impersonate the government, so top search results are not proof a site is official.
The FTC also cites misleading promises and fake reviews, so glowing ratings alone should not earn your trust.

sections.heading: Debt Relief Scheme Banned
bullets: A federal court permanently banned operators of an alleged debt relief scheme, following an FTC request.
The scheme allegedly targeted seniors and veterans, groups worth warning in your family.
Operators allegedly impersonated banks, credit card companies and government agencies to gain trust.
On October 14, 2026, the court entered a $106.8 million default judgment against corporate defendants.

sections.heading: FTC Report on Older Adults
bullets: The FTC sent Congress its report Protecting Older Consumers 2025-2026, built on fraud reports from older adults.
It highlights key fraud trends affecting older Americans, useful context for anyone helping aging parents.
The report details law enforcement actions against unfair or deceptive practices aimed at older consumers.

brief.seo_description: FTC sues alleged fake government passport help operators, a court bans a debt relief scheme targeting seniors, and a new FTC report on older adult fraud.
